message.content: The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is a small, probably omnivorous placental mammal that lived roughly 50–60 million years ago, during the late Paleocene–early Eocene. This ancestor would have been part of the early diversification of the clade that eventually split into the carnivoran lineage (leading to Felidae) and the perissodactyl lineage (leading to Equidae). It is not a named species, but rather a hypothetical ancestral form inferred from the fossil record and molecular phylogenies.
